facts.fact: UsdPrim::IsA<SomeSchemaClass>() returns true for any prim whose typeName is or derives from SomeSchemaClass.
The IsA schema a prim subscribes to is determined by its typeName metadata.

claims.claim: `prim.IsA<UsdGeomXformable>()` checks whether a Mesh prim's schema derives from `UsdGeomXformable`.
`prim.IsA(TfType(UsdGeomXformable))` is a valid alternative spelling of that check.
`UsdPrim::IsA` queries a prim's typed schema type.
`UsdPrim::HasAPI` checks whether a particular API schema is applied.
`IsA` and `HasAPI` have overloads that take a `TfType` representing the schema type.
`IsA` and `HasAPI` have forms templated on the C++ schema class.

facts.fact: By default, if the value type supports linear interpolation, Get() linearly interpolates between the time samples that bracket the requested time.
Calling UsdStage::SetInterpolationType(UsdInterpolationTypeHeld) forces all time samples on the stage to resolve with held interpolation.
Value types that cannot be interpolated, such as bool, always use held interpolation.

facts.fact: With sRGB the texture is read using the sRGB transfer curve, but not filtered against the sRGB gamut.
raw uses the texture data as read, and auto checks the file's metadata, falling back to sRGB for 8-bit 3- or 4-channel textures.

claims.claim: For UsdUVTexture's sourceColorSpace, the value sRGB describes only the transfer curve, not the gamut of the image.

facts.fact: A variant can contain overriding opinions for properties and metadata, as well as arbitrary scene description such as child prim subtrees.
Variants can also include additional composition arcs, such as references; changing the variant selection then controls which asset is referenced.

claims.claim: A variant can modify metadata on the prim that owns the variant set.
A variant can contain overriding opinions for properties, metadata, and more, as well as arbitrary scene description.
A reference can be added on a variant instead of on the prim itself in a variantSet.
In a stronger referencing context, another variant can be added to the variantSet to add a different reference.

facts.fact: The encoding of a .usd file can be specified with FileFormatArguments to SdfLayer::CreateNew or SdfLayer::Export.
Otherwise the USD_DEFAULT_FILE_FORMAT environment variable controls the default: unset or usdc gives Crate binary, usda gives UTF-8 text.

claims.claim: FileFormatArguments can explicitly specify the encoding of a .usd layer.
Without an explicit format argument, USD_DEFAULT_FILE_FORMAT controls the encoding of a new .usd layer.
When USD_DEFAULT_FILE_FORMAT is unset, a new .usd layer defaults to the random-access Crate binary format (usdc).

facts.fact: Variability (varying or uniform) is metadata that states intent; it is not consulted by the core during authoring or value resolution, to keep those fast.
Variability can be used for validation by higher-level authoring code, and as a hint that the value is not expected to change over time.

claims.claim: The file should not be rejected.
The attribute should be read as varying (not uniform).
Variability is not consulted or consumed by the USD core during authoring or value resolution, in order to keep those operations fast.

facts.fact: The varname input of UsdPrimvarReader is of type string (changed from token).
token is reserved for enum-like inputs with a fixed set of choices, and Material interface inputs such as inputs:frame:st should also be string valued.

claims.claim: The UsdPrimvarReader's inputs:varname should be authored as a string in current USD versions (2.2 and newer).

facts.fact: The usdz specification imposes no further constraints on package content, and packages can themselves contain other packages.

claims.claim: A usdz package can contain other usdz packages.

facts.fact: Default stage traversals terminate at instances, because instances are not allowed to have prim children; a client can reach the prototype through UsdPrim::GetPrototype.
Traversals can be given a predicate built from prim flags instead of the default predicate.

claims.claim: Instances are not allowed to have prim children.
Default stage traversals terminate at instances because instances are not allowed to have prim children.

facts.fact: Animation blocks block only animated values from weaker opinions, not default values, so the weaker default value still comes through.
An animation block is authored as `attr = AnimationBlock` in usda, or with UsdAttribute.BlockAnimation(), and applies to the whole attribute value.

claims.claim: An animation block can be created for a specific attribute to make it static while keeping its default value without editing the source file.
An animation block blocks animated values from a reference while allowing the default value to remain.
An animation block only blocks animated values (TimeSamples and Splines) and not default values.

facts.fact: To add a material binding, the MaterialBindingAPI schema must be applied to the prim, which is then bound via the material:binding relationship.
Validation includes a rule requiring MaterialBindingAPI to be applied to gprims that need to be bound to materials.

claims.claim: Applying the MaterialBindingAPI schema is required for a material binding to count.
The prims lack MaterialBindingAPI in their apiSchemas, which is why they no longer get their materials.
Excerpt 1 states: 'To add a material binding, the MaterialBindingAPI schema must be applied to a prim.'
Excerpt 2 states: 'Your Gprim must apply the MaterialBindingAPI API schema and bind the material via the :usda:`material:binding` relationship.'

facts.fact: The Alembic file format plugin collapses xform + shape combinations into a single transformable gprim in UsdGeom.
Gprims are transformable themselves, so a parent Xform just for transforming a Mesh is unnecessary; collapsing typically cuts prim counts by 40-50%.

claims.claim: The Alembic file format plugin collapses "xform + shape" combinations into a single "transformable gprim" in UsdGeom.

facts.fact: A stage is the USD scenegraph derived from a root USD file and all the referenced or layered files it composes, and it always presents the composed view.

UsdStage caches just enough about the composed namespace and backing files for fast traversal and queries, and allows edits targeted at any contributing layer; UsdStage::Save saves the changed layers.

claims.claim: A USD stage is the USD abstraction for a scenegraph derived from a root USD file and all of the referenced/layered files it composes.
A USD stage contains a composed view of the scene description.
A USD stage contains a tree of prims that form a namespace hierarchy.
A USD stage caches information about the composed namespace and backing files.

facts.fact: Out of the box USD supports the .usda, .usdc and .usd file formats, plus plugins for reading and writing Alembic and reading MaterialX files.
Other formats can be read only if a developer writes a file format plugin that translates them into the USD scenegraph.

claims.claim: USD does not reference OBJ files directly.
USD requires a plugin to read OBJ files.
The error message indicates that the necessary plugin is not found or not configured.

facts.fact: Nesting gprims under other gprims is considered invalid, and usdchecker warns about it.
The reason is that activation and visibility apply hierarchically and prune: if an ancestor gprim is deactivated or invisible, no descendant gprim can be made active or visible.

claims.claim: It is not valid to nest prims under a gprim.
A rule in OpenUSD states: "Do not nest gprims in namespace".
OpenUSD considers it invalid to nest gprims under other gprims.
Key features of USD such as activation and visibility apply hierarchically and are "pruning".
When an ancestor gprim is deactivated or made invisible, there is no possible way to make any descendant gprim active or visible.
